summary: Twenty-three existing SOC major-group link targets have individual provisional route screens. None is qualified for development or publication; public-query demand, group-to-role mapping, and commercial fit remain unresolved.
programme_note: Twenty-three linked SOC major-group routes have individual provisional records and blueprints; all remain unqualified pending role mapping, user-demand evidence, competitor/SERP review, and owner approval. Forty-two of 65 quota slots remain unassigned.
quota_and_next_batch: The occupation-classification quota is 65. The 23 candidates correspond to existing missing SOC major-group destinations linked from the current site; they are not counted as qualified development pages. Forty-two quota slots remain unassigned. Next: map each major group to existing role pages, inspect page-level overlap, and obtain first-party query evidence before any qualify/merge decision.

candidate_defaults.search_intent: Navigational and informational: identify the scope of the U.S. SOC major group {classification_code} ({classification_name}) and browse relevant KOV role listings. Phrasing is a hypothesis, not measured query demand.
intent_evidence: The site coverage audit records this exact destination as linked by 35 source pages with 105 href occurrences/variants. This is evidence of existing internal navigation paths only, not public search demand.
candidate_defaults.intended_audience: People browsing KOV's role directory who need to locate existing roles within the {classification_name} classification group; whether this group fits KOV's candidate-service audience is unverified.
candidate_defaults.geographic_relevance: The 2018 SOC is a U.S. occupational classification. Any English-language page must label that scope and must not imply the taxonomy is universal or equivalent to other national systems.

competitor_research.name: O*NET OnLine
competitor_research.finding: The U.S. Department of Labor resource describes browsing and profiles for 900+ occupations. It is an official occupational reference, not a direct executive-career competitor.
competitor_research.status: general reference page verified 2026-11-05; candidate-specific commercial competitor and Google/Bing SERP review pending

competitor_research.name: Direct commercial competitors and current search results
competitor_research.finding: No candidate-specific commercial competitor or search-result ranking was verified in this screen.

candidate_defaults.commercial_relevance: A group landing page could restore the intended route into existing role directories, but candidate-side service fit, conversion value, and demand are unverified. A taxonomy label must not imply that KOV provides services for every listed occupation.
candidate_defaults.unique_content_purpose: Provide a navigational landing page for the 2018 U.S. SOC major group {classification_code}, {classification_name}, and link only to KOV role pages whose mapping to this group has been individually checked. Do not copy the full SOC taxonomy or make a placement/service claim.
candidate_defaults.overlap_assessment: The exact linked destination is absent from the audited site, while the site already has 40 role indexes and 554 role-industry pages. A landing page is distinct only as a classification-based index; mapping existing roles, avoiding duplicate role descriptions, and verifying audience fit are unresolved. SOC is U.S.-specific.
factual_gaps_and_risks: Verify the current scope and title of SOC group {classification_code} against the locally validated 2018 SOC workbook and an accessible authoritative source before drafting.
Map existing KOV role pages to {classification_name}; no mapping has been asserted in this screen.
Review current role-page text and internal links for duplication; the classification destination itself is not a factual reason to create a commercial guide.
No Search Console, keyword-volume, difficulty, traffic, conversion, or actual Google/Bing SERP data is available.
Confirm audience fit and KOV serviceability; the U.S. SOC must not be presented as a global occupational taxonomy.
proposed_outline: Explain the limited U.S. 2018 SOC scope of {classification_code}, {classification_name}, and its difference from an industry classification.
List only existing KOV role pages whose mapping to this major group has been checked; mark missing role mappings rather than inventing examples.
Explain how visitors can use the role links without implying that classification membership predicts a career outcome or service eligibility.
Link to relevant KOV career-strategy information and state any geographic or terminology limits.
Include source date, classification edition, and a review trigger for taxonomy changes.
